$comment: The module's words (E65 C4; S18-31, S17-36): every term with its English and Polish, the Polish gender and inflection where a decision gives them, its forbidden variants and the stage from which it holds.

Who reads it: scripts/tests-text.mjs, through `node tools/check.mjs text` in Node - T8 (glossaryHits: a forbidden variant where an entry holds) and T28 (retiredHits: a retired name where it is retired); the writers of texts, from docs/text-style.md (E65 C5). Nothing at a table reads it (export-ignore).

The stage rule: an entry holds once its `stage` has shipped (tools/stages.mjs isShipped). An entry whose texts obeyed it when E65 measured it (31.10.2026) has the stage that brought the name, or E65 for a general rule; one T8 found broken has the stage that fixes it - E25 for D33a-D33f and DB residue, E66 for renamed names, E71 for Remnant in a sentence, American spelling, Search Token, the declension of loanwords (T12) and the texts of A8; the names of topics A, C and D the stage that brings them. T8 reports from E65 and fails from E25 (UI and config.mjs, stages up to E25), E71 and E57 (handbooks); T28 fails from E66.

A forbidden variant is a phrase or a stem with its endings, matched as a whole word, in the side's case (`case`: exact unless "any"), never inside the entry's own term or a phrase of `except`; `otherCase` finds the term in another case. `open: true` marks an entry no source read decides: it forbids nothing. A retired name comes back only by the owner's decision, and a stage that brings a new name fixes its entry and T28 in the same commit (the plan).

`declension` (E65 C7): what DB4 and D33c say of an entry's Polish forms, for T11 and T12 and for T18's countable nouns - `indeclinable: true`, or the forms it lists by case (gen, dat, instr, loc, plural) with `countable: true` for DB4's countable nouns (and the GM, D33c); `inflection` keeps the source's words.
Dashes are "-". Edited by hand; `node tools/check.mjs text` holds its shape (a schema error is red).
